title: Who Owns the Shelf: Black-Owned Brands and National Retailers | At The Margins, Ep. 5
lede: Black consumers made about 11% of U.S. beauty spending in 2021; Black-owned brands got about 2.5% of the revenue. Episode 5 of At The Margins follows a product onto a national retailer's shelf: slotting fees and payment terms, the 2020 pledges at Sephora, Target and Walmart and what's been reported since, Canada's pledges and the Hudson's Bay collapse, and what the evidence says helps small suppliers grow.
keyPoints: Black households are 13.1% of U.S. households and 11% of tracked spending; their spending grew 3.8% in 2025 vs 7.7% overall (NielsenIQ).
Beauty, 2021: Black consumers 11.1% of spending, Black brands 2.5% of revenue and under 7% of shelf products (McKinsey).
Slotting: $2,313 to $21,768 per product, per retailer, per metro area; $1.5–2M for a national launch (FTC, 2003, the latest federal study).
Sephora's Black-owned brands rose from ~3% in 2020 to ~10% in 2025 (CNBC); Target says its $2B commitment was completed (Axios); no major retailer publishes Black-owned brands' share of sales.
Paying small suppliers 15 days sooner raised payroll 10 cents per dollar (Barrot & Nanda, Journal of Finance).
